newsitem.title: INDONESIA: At least 1,200 said missing after Indonesia riots.
newsitem.headline: At least 1,200 said missing after Indonesia riots.

text.p: At least 1,200 people are missing due to ethnic riots that have rocked Indonesia's West Kalimantan province since December, a youth forum said on Wednesday.

Hidayat, chairman of the Indonesian Moslem Student Organisation (PMII), told Reuters a three-member team appointed by youth organisations visited West Kalimantan from February 7-14 to investigate and concluded 1,200 people were missing.

"We conducted an investigation in villages along an area stretching 60 km (37.5 miles) to 70 km around (West Kalimantan capital) Pontianak. We base our calculation regarding the missing people on the number of villagers who are still alive before and after the unrest," he said.

Hidayat said the forum could not say if the missing people had died. "We cannot find any evidence if the missing people are also the dead victims...even though we have discovered a body with a missing head there, for instance," he said.

Violence erupted in West Kalimantan, on the Indonesian side of Borneo island, late in December between members of the native Dayak tribe and migrants from Madura island, which lies off the main Indonesian island of Java.

The clash in Sanggau Ledo, about 95 km (60 miles) north of Pontianak, was apparently sparked by a fight over a girl. Further violence rooted in long-standing ethnic rivalry resumed in late January and continued as recently as last week. About 3,000 troops have been deployed to contain the unrest.
A military official in Pontianak said on Wednesday peace had returned to West Kalimantan and denied reports that five people had been killed in the coastal town of Singkawang recently.
Police said last week they had questioned 70 people accused of involvement in the rioting and would submit the dossiers of 11 to prosecutors.

Armed forces commander General Feisal Tanjung said last month the conflict had been ended by a peace pact signed by the warring parties. Most Dayaks are Christians while the Maduran migrants are Moslems, the dominant belief in the country.

Tanjung also denied reports that about 300 people had been killed in the riots and said he would soon announce the official death toll. Military officials and residents of the province had previously said at least 12 people had been killed over the past six weeks.
